text:
maria: heads-up — saw a ~22% drop in tokens/sec on the seq=1024 Llama-variant baseline after the runtime change landed last night. numbers from canary:
maria: run: `./bench --model llama-13b --kernel flash-v2 --seq 1024 --batch 8`
maria: tokens/sec: 78k -> 61k, p50 latency up from 58ms -> 72ms, gpu util stable ~86% though.
ajay: ugh. which change specifically? the kernel selector fallback? or batching heuristics tweak?
maria: looks correlated with the kernel-path heuristic that switches to paged attention when kv-cache > 5MB per request
kai: do we have perf counters for memory copies / L2 thrash? paged attention introduces extra gather ops that can bite at these shapes
maria: attached snippet from perf trace (simplified):
```
FlashV2::compute_attn  time=12.3ms
PagedAttn::gather     time=23.9ms  (+11.6ms vs baseline)
KVCache::evict_scan   time=3.1ms
Memcpy H2D            time=6.8ms
```
maria: so paged path is dominating when our heuristic flips for seq>800 with sparse kv hits
jen_bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout (kernel-selector v1.9) at 2026-12-31T02:14Z — health ok, perf alerts enabled
lucas: quick note: dollar-per-M-token went up ~18% for the affected routes because tokens/sec dropped but cost per-GPU stayed same
ajay: what are absolute $/M numbers? helps to prioritize.
lucas: pre-regression: $4.2 / M tokens; post: $5.0 / M tokens (batching policy unchanged)
kai: the classifier that picks paged vs fused uses kv_size_estimate heuristically; maybe underestimates locality and picks paged too often
maria: hypothesis: when batch mixes short and long sequences, selector misfires — long seq triggers paged kernel for entire micro-batch
ajay: timeline: yesterday's commit 0f9a3 changed selector to use max_seq in batch instead of per-item decision to reduce branching. maybe that caused over-eager paged selection
maria: can reproduce locally by interleaving short (128) and long (1024) requests in same batch — tokens/sec drops ~20%
kai: quick experiment idea: enable per-item kernel selection (exp) and measure overhead. if overhead < 2% but tokens/sec recovers 18% it's an easy win
lucas: any SLO impact? p99 tail for user-facing chat routes increased from 420ms -> 610ms, so yes customer-visible
ajay: safe rollback options: revert selector change, or change batching policy to homogeneous batches by seq (harder), or tweak threshold for paged path to seq>1400
maria: ran micro-bench with per-item selection enabled: tokens/sec back to 76k, p50 60ms. overhead in scheduler ~1.3%.
maria: patch proposal: switch to per-item kernel decision for now + add a batching refinement that groups by seq length when batching across requests
kai: followup: need to check KV cache behavior — per-item selection may increase kernel switches and kv cache locality could suffer; run kv-hit-rate monitor
jen_bot: monitoring-bot: new metric kv_select_mismatch_rate created; alert if >5% for 5m
lucas: cost calc: if we keep regression, monthly delta ~ $12k on prod hosts for this customer cohort. reversing saves that.
ajay: steps: (1) revert selector commit in canary, (2) enable per-item selection flag for 24h, (3) run 6-hour perf sweep including mixed-batch scenarios, (4) evaluate $/M tokens and p99
maria: I'll open PR with feature-flagged per-item selector + tests and attach perf-run scripts. will also add a unit that simulates mixed batches to CI.
kai: also suggest adding small microbench for memcpy and gather on target GPUs — might expose hardware-specific regression (A100 vs H100 diff)
lucas: pinging infra for a reserved 2-GPU canary for the 6-hour sweep
maria: thanks — will post results in this thread. for now, marking incident label: perf-regression-atten-kernel
ajay: nice triage team. :thumbsup:
